memoryText: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. This week you finished the wilderness books with the review of Unit 7, and you crossed the Jordan with Joshua. Take a quiet moment today to sit with the opening of Joshua. Read Joshua 1:1-9 again slowly if you can, and let the promise of God’s presence settle in.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Joshua 1:9 is a command wrapped around a promise, and the promise is what holds the command up.

“Have I not commanded you?” God begins with a reminder. He has already spoken. Joshua does not need a new word. He needs to believe the one he has.

“Be strong and courageous.” This is the third time in nine verses that the words appear. Courage is not a feeling that arrives on its own. It is a choice made in response to what God has said. Joshua will be afraid. God does not deny it. He commands courage because fear is real.

“Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed.” The two words describe fear that shakes you from the inside and discouragement that drains you from outside. Both are answered by the same thing.

“For the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.” This is the reason. Not “because you are strong,” not “because you are well prepared,” but because he is with you. Every step into unknown territory is accompanied.

Notice the last phrase: wherever you go. Joshua would go into the Jordan, into Jericho, into battle, and into long years of leadership. The promise follows him into all of it. And for the Christian, the promise is stronger still. Jesus said, “I am with you always, to the end of the age” (Matthew 28:20). Carry this verse into the places you dread this week.
weekInReview:
This week you finished the wilderness books with the Unit 7 review, spending time in Psalm 119, the long song of delight in God’s word. Then you began Unit 8 and the book of Joshua. You heard God commission a new leader and promise his presence. You met Rahab, the Canaanite woman who confessed that the LORD is God in heaven above and on earth beneath, and who hung a scarlet cord in her window. You watched the priests step into a flooded Jordan and saw the waters stop, you saw twelve stones piled up at Gilgal, and you saw a new generation circumcised and the Passover kept. You met the commander of the LORD’s army, and you sang Psalm 114, in which the sea flees and the mountains skip.

The week taught one lesson in many forms: God keeps his promises, and he goes before his people.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you most need courage right now? Joshua was not told to feel brave. He was told to be strong because God was with him. Name one situation where fear or discouragement is pressing on you, and write down what it would look like to take one faithful step in it this week.

How does Rahab’s story point you to Christ? She was an outsider under judgment, who heard about God’s works, believed, and took refuge in the way of rescue he provided. A scarlet cord marked her house, and she was brought into God’s people and into the line of the Messiah. How does her story clarify what it means that Jesus saves, not on the basis of who we are, but on the basis of what he has done?

What “memorial stones” help you remember what God has done? Think about the practices, places, or people that keep your faith anchored. Is there one you have neglected? What could you do this week to retell God’s faithfulness to someone else?
prayerPrompts: Rest in God’s promise to be with you wherever you go.
Thank him for Rahab, and for mercy that reaches outsiders like you.
Tell him what you are leaving in his hands this Sabbath.
